q: 1. The value of buckling load is ___ than crushing load in case of long column
explain: For long, slender columns, the Euler buckling load is reached well before the crushing (yield) load — that's precisely why long columns fail by buckling first.

q: 2. The effective length of a column effectively held in position and restrained in direction at one end will be
explain: As per the standard end-condition tables for this specific restraint case.

q: 3. Effective length of a column fixed at one end and hinged at the other end is
explain: Standard result: fixed-hinged effective length Le = L/√2 ≈ 0.707L.

q: 4. The equivalent length of a column fixed at one end and free at the other end, is
explain: Standard result: fixed-free (cantilever) effective length Le = 2L.

q: 5. The ratio of the effective length of a column and minimum radius of gyration of its cross-sectional area, is known as
explain: Slenderness ratio λ = Le/k_min, by definition.

q: 10. For a column of given material, the Rankine's constant depends on
explain: Rankine's constant (1/a = σc/π²E) depends only on the material's crushing stress and modulus of elasticity — not on the column's length, diameter, or moment of inertia.
A strut is defined by its function (carrying compression), not its orientation — it may be horizontal, vertical, or inclined.

q: 12. Compression members always tend to buckle in the direction of the
options: parallel to the axis of load
perpendicular to the axis of load
explain: Buckling occurs about the axis of least radius of gyration, since that's the weakest bending direction.

q: 13. The inclined member carrying compressive load in case of frames and trusses is
explain: An inclined compression member in a truss/frame is called a strut.
